title: Jupiter and the Monkey's Baby
text:
Jupiter, king of the gods, announced a contest among the animals. Every creature was to bring its offspring before his throne, and he would give a prize to the one judged the most beautiful.

The animals came in a long procession: the birds with their chicks, the deer with their fawns, the lions with their cubs. Among them came a monkey, carrying her baby in her arms with all a mother's tenderness. It was a flat-nosed, hairless, scrawny little creature.

When the monkey presented it, the gods burst out laughing. The mother monkey held her child closer and was not in the least embarrassed.

"Jupiter may give the prize to whomever he likes," she said. "But I know that in my own eyes this is the dearest, handsomest and most beautiful of all."
lesson: Every parent sees their own child through love. It is a good thing at home, but remember that others see with different eyes.
